seoTitle: Gzip Inspector: Header, CRC-32 and Compression Ratio
metaDescription: Read the header of a .gz file (name, time, OS, flags), verify its CRC-32 and size by decompressing in the browser, and see the compression ratio.
intro: Check a gzip file's metadata and integrity without a command line.
why:
The inspector parses the header fields from RFC 1952: flags, modification time, original file name, comment, extra field, compression level hint and operating system. It then decompresses the data with the browser's DecompressionStream, computes the CRC-32 of the result and compares it and the size with the trailer.

Brotli (.br) files cannot be read because browsers do not expose a Brotli decompressor to pages. Files with several members or sizes over 4 GB report the size field modulo 2^32.

The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
howTo: Read the header and integrity result.
Compare the ratio with other compression settings.
Re-create the file if the CRC does not match.

faq.q: What does a CRC mismatch mean?
faq.a: The data was corrupted, truncated or modified after compression.

faq.q: Does it show the original name?
faq.a: If the compressor stored one. Many tools, such as gzip -n or servers, omit it.
It verifies and measures; use the gzip decompress tool to get the content.
The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
